utterances.text: Yes. One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are all in agreement here that it falls within the parameters of the cross-examination. Go ahead, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let me just say that again and maybe rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Are you aware now that a thousand or over a thousand Muslims were murdered in the area between Konjevic Polje and Kravica on 13 July and buried in the nearby vicinity?

utterances.speaker: MILE SIMANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean now, at the moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILE SIMANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could learn that from the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you think it's true?

utterances.speaker: MILE SIMANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not up to me to establish that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. Judge Kwon. Judge Stole? We don't have any further questions for you, Mr. Simanic, which means you're free to go. Our staff will give you all the assistance you require. On behalf of my colleagues, Judge Kwon, Judge Prost and Judge Stole, I wish to thank you for having come over to give testimony, and we also wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Documents or exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, the 14 July document is already in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is already in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: 2627. I don't know if you want to see the original inked marks that we referred to around the diesel, but you're welcome to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That will always be available in case we need to see it, won't it, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Of course, of course. I also have the 12 July combat report that shows the location of the signature on that last point I made on redirect. We can put that into evidence. It doesn't have a 65 ter number, if you think it's necessary, or we can just rely on the record. I think it's probably safer just to put it in evidence, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any comments from the Defence? Any objections? Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no objections, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So those two -- one is already admitted, it's already on the record, and this last one will be admitted and given a number. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We do have a number from Ms. Stewart. It's 2882.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 2882, okay, thank you. Any of the Defence teams wish to tender any documents? Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We would like to tender the document 1D379. It was used. It's a Drina Corps collection -- overview of existing troops accounted for Drina Corps in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I take it counsel is agreeing to the authenticity of that document, or at least arguing for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would leave that to become a submission later on, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, without such, I would object, because there has to be some point of authenticity. Counsel just can't bring material in from -- and then say nothing about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This document was taken from the collection of the Prosecution, from the EDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I guess I'll have to be satisfied with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objections? None, so that document is admitted. Any further documents from any of the Defence teams? Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have two documents to tender. This is 4D50006 and 4D -- which is the order by Radovan Karadzic, and 4D0007, which is the dispatch that was sent by the Minister of the Interior on the 23rd of March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Stojanovic, let's clear this. Are you tendering two or three, because the transcript may be misleading. We have two documents to tender, you said, and then you have the first one, which is 4D50006, and then 4D, and we have a blank, 4D, and then 4D0007. But to make it clear, you're tendering only two?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, and this is P0006 and 4DP00007. Those are the numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could just -- I see they have ERNs on them, meaning they are Prosecution-oriented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we just hear, just to save us some time, what collection they're from, because I'm afraid I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: They're your 6 and 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. If that's been a Prosecution exhibit, no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, if it has a "P" already, I think it -- exactly. All right. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And from the Defence, other Defence teams, no objections? So those two documents are also so admitted. I don't think there is anything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Entirely neutral about this document, Your Honour; happy for it to go in, if the Trial Chamber would like it to. It's a Prosecution document, but we're not pressing for it to be admitted, but we certainly have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't remember which document that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we might as well have it in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'm happy to arrange for it to go in with a "6D" number. I suspect it will be 6DP0019 [sic]. Ms. Cmeric is confirming that that's right. I'm grateful to her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So that will be so admitted with a "6D" identification number. Any further documents? None. So that closes the testimony of Mile Simanic. We now come to PW-108. We will need to bring down the curtains. I'm informed, and it is correct information, that to install the voice distortion equipment will require a few minutes, so five minutes? How much? I know they usually ask for 20 minutes, but I don't think they will require 20 minutes, although that would be very welcome for Mr. Meek and Mr. Bourgon. Let's have a short break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. The suggestion is that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. The suggestion is that we have the break now, 25 minutes, in other words, during which time they will install the equipment, and then we start after that and continue until we finish. All right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, I think Mr. Bourgon would like to tell you something.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I was wondering, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you want to approach him, please do, by all means. I think it will be easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I was expecting flowers, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think I overheard, more or less, what you said from here, even with the headphones on. Is there a need for the application of 90 E or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I do not see one, Mr. President. I'm being advised that my friend disagrees so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But then if there is disagreement, we give the caution; agreed?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: That is much more simple, because my colleague was suggesting to -- for me to explain why with the witness not being in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We will be applying 90 E, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning -- or good afternoon to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome to this courtroom. You are about to start giving evidence very soon. Before you do so, you're required by our Rules to undertake to testify the truth. The text of this solemn declaration that is required from you is going to be handed to you now. Please read it out aloud, and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is his microphone --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is his microphone switched off? Okay. Sir, it's very important that whenever you see a microphone -- somebody else's microphone with the red light on, that you don't speak. Let me explain. Please make yourself comfortable, in the first place. Have a seat, and I'll explain the rest. At the special request of the Prosecution, we have put in place for you some protective measures. The first one is facial distortion, the second is voice distortion, and the third is an application of a pseudonym instead of using your real name and surname. These, I suppose, have been explained to you. I just want to make sure from you that you're happy with this arrangement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So before we proceed, what's going to happen is that Mr. Thayer will go first, and he will ask you some questions, and then he will be followed by various members of the Defence teams. Now, in the course of your testimony, it is possible, although I'm not suggesting that it is going to happen, but it is possible that questions might be or may be put to you which, if you answer truthfully, could potentially expose you to criminal proceedings. Again, I don't know if this is going to happen, but I have to work on the assumption that this could happen. In case you are asked such incriminatory questions, you have a right to draw our attention, the Judges here, and ask that you be exempted from providing an answer to those questions. We have two options, and that's because your right is not absolute. One option for us is to agree with you and grant you exemption from answering such questions. Another option is exactly the opposite. We may not agree with you at all, and we may decide to compel you to answer such questions. If we do so, however, unless your answer constitutes false testimony, then you have a further guarantee, a further right; namely, that whatever you answer in reply to such incriminatory questions will not be used against you in any possible future criminal proceedings that could be instituted against you. Have I made myself sufficiently clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I think on that basis, we can now start the examination-in-chief. I remind you all of two things. One is there will not be a further break now, we'll go straight to quarter to 2:00. The second thing is since we have put in place the protective measure of voice distortion, it is important that as soon as you finish putting your questions, you switch off your microphone, and if at any time the witness speaks, even if it's not in reply to any question, please make sure that all other microphones are switched off. Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, with Madam Usher's assistance, I'm going to hand you a piece of paper, and I would like you just to read the piece of paper and confirm that your name is on that piece of paper next to the pseudonym "PW-108."

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That will remain sealed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And for the record, Mr. President, that is P02881. And while it's being distributed, if we can may go into private session for a few questions, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session now, so we proceed along the lines that we have indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, in July of 1995, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: On one occasion, I did, when my friend came one morning to see me and asked me to go with him to Mr. Pandurevic in Zvornik. And he also asked me that I should drive him in my car. I said that we were forbidden to cross into another republic, and then he said to me that he would justify it, justify me going across with him, he would square it. When we crossed, we went to the barracks and looked for Mr. Pandurevic. He wasn't there in the barracks, except we found Mr. Nikolic at one point in the barracks, and we said hello, and my friend went off with Mr. Nikolic to an office and I stayed behind in the corridor to wait for them to finish their talk. Later on, after about some 10 to 15 minutes, my friend came out with Mr. Nikolic, out of the office. We said goodbye and started off back to where we had come from, across the way. On our return, my friend was not in a good mood, and he said that they were doing all sorts of things and that only madmen could do that kind of thing, and he wasn't in a good mood. He didn't comment anymore, but when we returned, he left for Belgrade. While we were going back on our return, he mentioned Mr. -- my friend Mr. Beara, whom I never heard of, saw, or knew. All he did was to comment and say that he was involved, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Let me back up a little bit and ask you some follow-up questions. When your friend first approached you and asked you to accompany him, can you describe what his mood or his demeanour was like when he approached you and on the trip to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: My friend was otherwise always in a good mood and smiling, but he would never comment on any events. It was only at that point when we were leaving that he seemed depressed and said that I should go and check out what was happening over there. And he was worried the whole time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did he tell you anything about why he wanted to go across and see Vinko Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: I assume in order to learn something more, to get some more information from him, and that he could influence something that I don't know about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek. Please be careful, because we will need to block that part of the transmission. I mean, I'm trying to keep my eyes wide open all the time to watching everywhere. Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and I apologise. I object. That question obviously leads to speculation. This is a fact witness. He's not here to assume or believe. He's here to say what he saw or what he heard or what he observed. And absolutely my objection is that calls for speculation, and I'd like the answer stricken also, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question, I don't even think I need to consult with my colleagues. The question did not ask for any speculation at all. The question was: "Did he tell you anything about why he wanted to go across and see Vinko Pandurevic?" And then he answered: "I assume in order to learn something more, to get some more information from him, and that he will influence something that I don't know about. Now, what I'm going to do is I'm going to go directly to the witness and ask him whether he is speculating or whether he is making this statement based on some conclusion that he reached at the time. But the question itself did not call for speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I appreciate that, but the answer was non-responsive to the question, and the answer only called for a yes-or-no answer. It was absolutely non-responsive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If the answer was to be "yes," he would have been expected to amplify straightaway on that and explain what his friend might have told him, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let us handle it. I think the message is clear enough. Witness, look at me, please. Mr. Thayer, a few moments ago, put to you a very straightforward question relating to your friend, and he asked you: "Did your friend tell you anything about why he wanted to go to the place where you went to see Vinko Pandurevic?" And your answer was not, "Yes, he did tell me something, this is what he told me ...," your answer was: "I assume in order to learn something more, to get some more information from him, and that he could influence something that I don't know about." This statement that you have just made to Mr. Thayer's question, is it a supposition, are you just speculating, or are you making a statement based on the conversation that you exchanged with your friend before you went to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I made the statement in the way that I considered was proper in answering the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I can follow up, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I won't. I think I have done enough. It's your baby now. Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just ask you to caution the witness that he's not here to assume or speculate. That's all I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, that we can do. In answering your questions, Witness, please make sure that if you are not sure, if you don't know, you don't try to speculate. However, when you know, then you proceed and answer the question. Thank you. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you stated in your answer that you assumed that your friend had wanted to learn something more, to get more information from Mr. Pandurevic. Now, I want you to think very carefully about the conversation that you had with your friend when he first approached you and anything he told you on the trip to this place. Can you tell the Trial Chamber, as best as you can remember, exactly what your friend told you? You said that he was worried. If you can remember what, if anything, he said about what he was worried about.

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: My friend said that he was worried and that something was happening across over there, (redacted) (redacted), so across, and that's why he was going to see Mr. Pandurevic, to receive additional information as to what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did he communicate to you whether this something that was happening was something that he considered to be good or something that he considered to be bad, or did he not say?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: He said that something bad was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I just want to ask you a few questions before we resume talking about your actual visit. At this time, at the time that you made this trip, what information did you have about the military situation in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: Well, Srebrenica was under siege, in an encirclement, and there were a lot of citizens in Srebrenica who were not able to leave Srebrenica and go anywhere because it was under a blockade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, what information did you have at that time about the whereabouts of the Muslim men from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: At that time when it was under a blockade, there were men, women and children in Srebrenica, and nobody could leave Srebrenica because it was under a blockade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Now, in July of 1995, when you made this trip, and again I don't want you to identify any personal information, but did you become aware of anyone from Srebrenica being transported anywhere?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment before you answer that question. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is a leading question. The witness is here to say what he saw or what he remembers, and the question should be open-ended and should not suggest to the witness, as in this case where he is suggesting to the witness that people from Srebrenica were being transported. That's a leading question and it suggests an answer to the witness and should not be permitted, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, we are all in agreement here that the question is perfectly legitimate. However, we would like you to rephrase it. Instead of saying, "Did you become aware," you rephrase it leaving for options, because that "but" over there can be on the margin between a leading question and a regular one. You need to rephrase your question, basically.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, at or about this time when you took this trip, what, if anything, did you observe regarding anyone being transported from anywhere?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon. That's very vague.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I mean, the same objection, Mr. President. Again, he's suggesting that people are being transported. He has to ask the witness what the witness saw or what the witness didn't see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the thing is he can definitely ask the witness, "Did you at any time become aware that people were being transported?" Of course, he can ask that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I believe, Mr. President, that this is a leading question. To ask, "Did you see if people were transported," suggests that people may have been transported.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, he can answer that with a "yes," a "no" or a number of ways.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please rephrase your question along the lines that I indicated. Ask the question. He has the right to put the question. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Or the witness can answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And now the witness has heard enough he's in a position to know what we're talking about. Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's my point. I don't know if the witness speaks English. We can ask him. If he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In any case, he's receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: He should take his headphones off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but he has been receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: From this point on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. From this point on, we can ask him. Do you understand English, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Can I kindly ask you to remove your headphones for a short while? I understand that Mr. Meek wants to make a submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek. Did you wish to add anything or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I don't wish to add anything now. I'm just saying the next objection, if there is one, or continuing from this point on, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Although I do agree with my colleague, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, I misunderstood you. It's okay, he can put back. Yes, you can put the question again, Mr. Thayer, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, during this period of time that we're talking about in July of 1995, do you recall seeing anyone being taken anywhere?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, who is "anyone"? Who is he talking about? If he does mention those people -- there's a way to ask these questions in a very simple manner, but right now he's not doing it properly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why didn't you return to your previous question, which had the blessing of the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I thought that we -- that I was going to be treading, if I asked the question I thought that I had asked, but if I can ask about transportation, then I will just simply repeat that question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you already received the blessing--

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- the go-ahead, and that would eliminate objections if you repeat the same question that we have already granted you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, during this period of time in July of 1995, when you took this trip, do you recall whether or not you saw anyone being transported anywhere?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: One could see a convoy of vehicles, buses and lorries that transported citizens. This was at the very entrance into Zvornik from the direction of Bratunac and Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we may move into private session for one question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall what time of the day it was when you set off on this trip?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: It was before the noon on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall where the Zvornik Brigade barracks were located, in what kind of facility?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: I believe it was a shoe factory called "Standard" in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived at Standard, to whom did you or your friend speak first?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: His first contact was with the soldier who was in the corridor. He was on guard duty. We looked for Mr. Vinko Pandurevic, who wasn't there. There were no other officers, either. That's when we came across Mr. Nikolic, and this is whom we spoke to, as I've just told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, this soldier who was on guard duty, did he appear to you to be an ordinary soldier or did he appear to you to be any kind of an officer?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: He was a foot soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And after you had spent a little bit of time in these barracks, did you notice anything about them?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: Well, the facility was empty, there was nobody there, and we did not notice anything else in addition to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were you directed anywhere in particular by this foot soldier?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: At that moment, Mr. Nikolic either came out of his office or just came by. We greeted him. Nikolic asked us what we were doing there. And then he entered Mr. Nikolic's office and I remained standing in the corridor, and I really don't know what the two were talking about in the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you recall whether -- or what floor of the barracks this encounter with Mr. Nikolic occurred, ground floor or first floor?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: The first floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, when you were upstairs, do you recall -- you just mentioned Mr. Nikolic's office. Do you recall whether that office was marked in any way, or how is it that you identify that as Mr. Nikolic's office?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether this was his office or not. Maybe he entered somebody else's office. I only know that that office was the first to the left next to the landing. I'm not sure whether this was his office or somebody else's.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And this man who introduced himself as Nikolic, could you see whether he had any rank?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: No, he did not have any patches. He was wearing a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you notice anything unusual about his uniform or the state of his uniform at that time?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: No. I believe that this was a work uniform, but I didn't notice anything special about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May we move into private session for one or two questions, please, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session, please, for a short while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you testified that your friend appeared to you to be worried about something bad that might have been happening. I want you to think as carefully as you can and tell the Trial Chamber, as best as you can remember, what, if anything, your friend said to Mr. Nikolic before they went into that office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment before you answer the question. Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: My objection, Your Honour, is this question has already been asked and answered. We ploughed that ground, and now he wants to go back over it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: The same objection, Mr. President. There was no mention of any conversation or anything that was said before going into the office. In fact, the witness was quite clear in terms of what happened when he met allegedly with Mr. Nikolic, that they went into the office and he did not hear anything. To go back before the going into the office is inappropriate, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, I think you need to address the point in a different manner. First you need to ask the witness to repeat or confirm whether before your friend entered into the office with Mr. Nikolic, there was any conversation, and whether he overheard that conversation. I think we need to start from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, before Mr. Nikolic and your friend entered the office, do you recall whether or not anyone, that is, Mr. Nikolic or your friend, said anything to the other that you were able to hear? And if so, what was it?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: Before they entered the office, after they greeted each other and after I greeted Mr. Nikolic, my friend's comment was this: "What are you doing? What is it that you're doing?" And then they entered the office. The door closed behind them, and I did not overhear any conversation coming from inside the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how long, approximately, did they remain in the office, sir?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: Fifteen minutes or so. Anything between 10 and 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you just generally describe the area in which you remained during this meeting?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: I remained in the corridor on the first floor, where Mr. Pandurevic's office also is and where they entered the office on the left-hand side. I was pacing the corridor while the two were talking. The barracks where we were, the whole facility was empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you see them come out of the office?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: When they ended their conversation, I saw them. We greeted each other again, and then we left the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you return directly to -- in the direction in which you came?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that your friend had wanted to find some more information about these bad things that might have been happening, and you mentioned that he mentioned the name Beara and that this Beara had been involved in some way. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Judge, this is very improper. All he's doing is repeating the testimony. It's ridiculous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's not ridiculous at all. Go ahead, Mr. Thayer, and come straight to your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. That's just where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did Mr. -- did your friend give you any indication of who mentioned this name Beara, how it came up in this conversation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Judge, that question is improper because it assumes facts not in evidence. There's been testimony that the friend had come and picked him up in the morning and had learned some things, and now that question assumes -- and again I thought we had a ruling that the witness would take the headphones off, but maybe it's too late. But that assumes facts not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What is not in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That anything about Mr. Beara was mentioned in that office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's what precisely the witness stated earlier on, what did his friend tell him after the meeting. But, anyway, I leave the question to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'm simply trying to clarify what the source of this name was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly, and in answering that question we would know whether the name of Beara was mentioned during the conversation between those two individuals or from some other source.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, from your conversation with your friend on the trip back, can you remember what, if anything, he told you about who mentioned this name Beara in the meeting?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: He mentioned Beara's name in this context: His comment was that it seems that Beara was also involved in all that. However, he did not tell me who had told him anything to that effect and based on which he mentioned this name. He did not say that Mr. Nikolic mentioned Beara's name. In any case, this is what he told me on our way back, that Beara is also involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, again, please put yourself back on that trip, on that return trip. What else, if anything, if you can remember in any more detail, did your friend tell you was happening that was bad?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: Another comment of his on our way back was that only lunatics and insane minds could be doing that, but he did not go into any detail, he did not explain what he meant by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did he mention any place where this -- these bad things were happening?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment before you answer the question. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness just said, "He did not go into any detail, he did not explain what he meant by that." Now my friend is again leading him and through what is -- might be mentioned in the interview that this witness gave to the Prosecution a long time ago, but this is improper examination, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber decision is to allow the question. The fact that he said he did not go into any detail does call for further questions, such as the one that has been put, to ensure that nothing and absolutely nothing else was stated. Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, on this trip back, think carefully. Do you recall whether your friend was able to provide you with any more detail about where these bad things were happening, based on that meeting he had?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: He did not say what was going on. He just mentioned several schools where prisoners were being kept, but he did not say what exactly was going on at those schools. He mentioned Karakaj, Rocevic and another name, maybe Celopek. I'm not sure what else he mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, did your friend tell you whether or not he was going to try to contact anyone else in connection with these bad things that he had heard were happening?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, asked and answered. He's now twice said, "This is all he told me. He didn't say anything else." And it's just repetitive and it's leading and suggestive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Meek, the previous answer proves exactly how right we were when we allowed the question, because it was obvious from his answer that the previous answer, namely, there was -- "He didn't give me any other detail," was not a precise one. So let's proceed, please, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. May I ask the witness to take his ear phones off, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sure. Sir, could you remove your ear phones, please? Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, at the beginning of this trial, the Trial Chamber issued some guidelines with respect to the evidence, saying that the Trial Chamber would not intervene with respect to leading questions unless this was raised by the parties. For most of this trial, we never intervene with leading questions, do we rarely do it. Mr. President, I believe it is important that when we do, that it is being enforced by the Trial Chamber. Leading questions are not permissible during examination-in-chief, and in this case, my colleague, even though there might be something else he said, there is a clear suggestion that he may have said something in relation to warning someone about what was happening. This is a clear suggestion -- a clear reminder to the witness to say something that exists in a document that all of us here are aware and the Trial Chamber. That's the part, Mr. President, that we are objecting to. He simply can say, "What else you say --" he could ask the question, "You say, 'I don't know what else he said,' but what else did he say? Tell me everything you remember about he said," period. He's not supposed to say and to lead him into every specific aspect of what he may have said. What matters to us is what the witness remembers today as he testifies before this Trial Chamber. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. Mr. Thayer, do you wish to respond to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, I think my position is clear, and I think the Court's reasoning is clear on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just need to consult my colleagues on whether the question needs to be rephrased, and we'll hand down our decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Our position about this, Mr. Bourgon, and it's unanimous, Mr. Bourgon, Mr. Thayer, it's a unanimous decision that you need to rephrase the question since that -- it should be something like this: "After having told you all this, did he in any way tell you whether he was going to do anything about what he had heard or on the information that he had received or not?"

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, I'll just read your question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, after having told you all this, did your friend in any way tell you whether he was going to do anything about what he had heard, or based on the information that he had received, or not?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: He said he'd try to intervene with some individuals, but he didn't say who he would try and contact, whether in Belgrade or Zvornik. He just confirmed that he would intervene to prevent anything bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was this the only trip you and your friend took to this place?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: Well, later on we went one more time looking for Vinko and Obrenovic, but we didn't find either of them, so we returned. And we were there once again several months later, my friend and I, when he commented and said that when he went home to (redacted), since the school was next to the road, that he saw a head cut off, a cut-off head, and he didn't make any more comments about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think we need a redaction, but I see you're on top of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As I told you, I think you should trust us with doing this whenever we feel it necessary. We are redacting the words that would be indicative of his origin.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir -- Mr. President, if we may go into private session for one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you mentioned a second trip in which you returned to Zvornik. Do you remember approximately how much time had passed between your first trip and this second trip?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: After a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, by the time of your second trip, what information, if any, had you heard concerning the fate of the Muslim men from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: Well, we didn't have any information about what was happening then.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you ever receive any information that there had been mass executions of men in the Zvornik area?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: We learnt of that later on in the ensuing period when the public got to know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber how soon the public began to learn about those mass executions in the Zvornik area?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember exactly how much time went by.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall what the purpose of this second trip was?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: The same purpose; that my friend should gain more information about what was happening next in the Zvornik area, but he didn't comment about what.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was your friend trying to do, sir, in obtaining this information, based on what he told you?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: I think he wanted to prevent all the bad things, and he condemned any crime if it occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, this meeting that your friend and Mr. Nikolic had, was that a friendly, an unfriendly, or a neutral meeting?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has already testified he wasn't involved in the meeting, so this question is purely speculative. He said he wasn't in there. He was in the hallway and he didn't know what they talked about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think it's very easy to handle. Please rephrase your question, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And ask the witness whether, after the meeting, whether his friend told him whether this was a friendly, unfriendly, or a neutral meeting, if he said any words to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Then my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: With all due respect, then my objection is: It's been asked and answered. Earlier, he said he was not in a good mood, he always used to smile, and on the way back he was grumpy, he wasn't in a good mood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And this is precisely why the question is perfectly legitimate, because of what he stated earlier. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did you understand His Honour's question? After the meeting that your friend had with Mr. Nikolic, did your friend tell you at any time on the ride back or any other time whether it was a friendly, an unfriendly, or a neutral meeting that they had?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: He did not say any one of those things, nor did he comment, but he was worried and depressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned another trip that you took across -- that you took to the same place. What was the purpose of that trip?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: For clarification, is this the second --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The second or the third, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Then I object. It's been asked and answered, page 87, line 22 through 25 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let Mr. Thayer tell us exactly which trip he is referring to. Which trip are you referring to, the last one?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The last one, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The last one, okay. So, you see, you need to be patient, Mr. Meek, like we are. Yes. We're referring to the last trip which you took some months later, and the question is whether you know what the purpose of that last trip was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With my friend -- I was with my friend. I didn't go to Zvornik, I didn't travel to Zvornik, but when we socialised on one occasion, he commented and said that when my friend (redacted) by the road in Rocevici, you have the primary school there, and in passing by, he saw a cut-off head. I wasn't travelling with him at the time, but he related that event to me or, rather, what he noticed when he was passing by his native village. But he did not say whose head it was, I assume, nor who the perpetrator was of that act.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did your friend indicate to you when or during what time period he saw this occur at the school?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: He did not say exactly when that was. I assume that it was earlier on, that is, before our meeting, before we socialised, so it was after the second or perhaps the first time we went to the barracks that that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. I want to show you a photograph that you've seen previously and my friends have seen. If we may look at P02880.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, if it may speed things up, we're ready to stipulate that the picture that you will show him, that the witness will identify Mr. Nikolic in that picture. Thank you, Mr. President, because I want to start today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know what picture it is, obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: It's a picture, Mr. President, that identifies a number of officers from the Zvornik Brigade. It's taken, I believe, somewhere in Zvornik, and it's not on the 65 ter list, but I'm perfectly willing to stipulate that -- first of all, to accept, even though it's not on the 65 ter list and that he will identify Mr. Nikolic on that picture. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. Mr. Thayer, do you still wish to show the picture to the witness or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I do, Mr. President. There are perhaps other people that he will be able to identify in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, fair enough. Let's proceed. Thank you, Mr. Bourgon, in any case. Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Judge, just on that last comment of my colleague, I'm going to object to him identifying any other individuals, because it would go beyond the 65 ter summary of what this witness was supposed to testify about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am not prepared to bet on that. Go ahead, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you see a photograph in front of you? I just need an answer. Do you see a photograph --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is waiting for the interpretation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recognise anyone in the photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you indicate, simply by indicating the position in the photograph, anyone you recognise?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: I recognise Mr. Nikolic. He is the fourth on the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just to be on the safe side, if we could have some assistance from Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, if you would just write the letter "N" above the head of the individual you've identified as Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: Here. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, during this period of time, what was the first name by which you knew this individual name, Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: I knew him as "Dragan" or "Drago," but more as "Dragan."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recognise anyone else in this photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: I recognise Mr. Pandurevic in the middle, and the second from the left is Mr. Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If you would just write the letter "P" above the head of Mr. Pandurevic and the letter "O" above the head of Mr. Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, if you would just write "P-108" anywhere on any of the corners and put today's date, which is the 4th of September, please.

utterances.speaker: PW-108.
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think we can save the exhibit. And, sir, I have no further questions for you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I offered to go faster. We did not take this route. I think while we have the picture there, my colleague should at least be -- do what he said and say does he recognise anybody else in that picture, and maybe we can save some time in cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think the question was: "Do you recognise anyone else in this photo?" And the gentleman said -- mentioned just two names.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, on many occasions, he stated something about a meeting and we went ten questions later to get more information. I think my colleague could just ask him does he recognise anybody else in the picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'll ask the question myself and bring this to an end. Do you recognise anyone else in this photo, apart from Nikolic, Pandurevic and Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just by sight. Between Obrenovic and Pandurevic, the person, I know that person, but I don't know this person's name. I just know the person by sight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There are three persons between Pandurevic and Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which one are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Standing in the first row with the moustache.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know anybody else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. You're finished with your in-chief. There's no point in even trying to start any cross-examination at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can I ask a question before cross-exam starts tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, you said today that your friend told you to the effect that it seems Mr. Beara was also involved. I note in particular the word "also." Does it mean that somebody else is originally involved? So if you could tell me now whether you heard anything from your friend or what your understanding was, whether somebody was originally involved.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He did not say that. At that moment, he only said that it seemed that Mr. Beara was also involved in all that. However, he did not mention anybody else who might have been involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, sir. You can now withdraw. We will resume with your testimony tomorrow morning. In the meantime, between now and then you are not to discuss anyone or allow anyone to approach you on the subject matter of your testimony. It is continuing tomorrow morning. When is the videolink?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Tomorrow morning, Mr. President, so we'll have to hold over the cross, I think as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see. I understand why Mr. Bourgon was standing up. Yes, okay. So we'll see you again, sir. We need to bring down the curtains while he exits the courtroom. Mr. Bourgon, I think you just wanted to confirm that we are going to proceed with the videolink tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Actually, Mr. President, I wanted to save some time and begin right now with one of my questions so we can leave the flavour with what's going on, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, we need to know what's going to happen tomorrow, because we also need to prepare ourselves. Tomorrow, are we having the videolink?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the cross-examination of this gentleman will be postponed until after?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And then we will pick up with Witness 101 at the conclusion of the cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that will probably take us through Friday, I would imagine, given the time estimates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. How long do you expect your in-chief tomorrow to last?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: To be on the safe side, I better estimate two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but then we only have -- but there is an estimate of two hours, 40 minutes by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes. We're prepared -- we've prepared with the site to go into Thursday, if we need it

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay, I thank you so much, and we will reconvene tomorrow morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 5th of September, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
